scope_summary: Prime coat application for bare drywall ceilings AND walls together in new construction, pre-trim phase. Single combined primer application covers both surfaces. No edge work required since same coat covers ceiling and wall continuously. Includes protection of windows, exterior doors, recessed lighting, and electrical boxes. Floor protection NOT required (subfloor only in NC pre-trim).
relevant_findings: Full prime (ceilings + walls together) eliminates edge work at ceiling line - both surfaces receive same primer coat
Pre-trim phase means no trim edge work required - baseboard/casing not yet installed
Spray+backroll is the production standard for NC full prime - enables fast coverage of large combined surface area
PVA primer is the standard for NC drywall - economical, fast-drying, excellent sealing
Gravity drip management: always prime ceilings FIRST, then walls to prevent drip contamination
Recessed lighting cans require protection from overspray - stuff with paper or use can covers
Electrical boxes (outlets, switches, junctions) require paper stuffing and tape to prevent insulation blow-out during spray
Windows and exterior doors in NC require plastic film masking before spray application
Maintain wet edge at ceiling-to-wall transition to prevent lap marks even without formal edge work
Drywall dust is primary contamination concern - HEPA vacuum all surfaces before priming
Floor protection NOT needed in NC pre-trim - subfloor only, no finished flooring to protect
Fastener spot-priming NOT required - galvanized screws do not rust during normal NC timeline; rust bleed-through is water damage scenario

clarifications_from_field.rationale: Galvanized drywall screws do not rust during normal mudding/priming timeline. Rust bleed-through only occurs from water damage left unchecked. If drywall contractor uses non-galvanized nails that rust during finishing, that is drywall contractor liability, not painting contractor scope.
NC pre-trim phase has subfloor only. No finished flooring to protect. Subfloor protection is not necessary.
Per-fixture count is unrealistic for estimating. Use room count with average fixtures per room (typically 4-8 cans per room in NC).

rationale: Gravity causes drips and splatter to fall downward
Primer drips from ceiling work will contaminate wall surfaces
Priming ceilings first allows any drips to be covered by subsequent wall priming
Backroller on ceiling must complete before wall spray begins
surface_sequencing.wet_edge_notes: At ceiling-to-wall transition, maintain wet edge to prevent lap marks. This is technique, not formal edge work.

ceiling_edge.reason: Same primer coat covers both ceiling and wall - no color break, no need for cut line

trim_edge.reason: Pre-trim phase - baseboard, casing, and crown not yet installed

corner_edge.reason: Inside corners are sprayed/rolled continuously, no special treatment

common_failure_modes.cause: Improper sequencing (walls primed before ceiling complete)
common_failure_modes.prevention: Always complete ceiling prime before starting walls
common_failure_modes.remediation: Sand drips smooth after dry, touch up with primer

common_failure_modes.prevention: Complete masking of all openings before spray begins
common_failure_modes.remediation: Scrape/clean affected surfaces, may require glass cleaning

common_failure_modes.cause: Boxes not protected, paint enters during spray
common_failure_modes.prevention: Stuff with paper and tape over face before spray
common_failure_modes.remediation: Remove paint from box interior, may require electrician

common_failure_modes.cause: Cans not protected, paint enters during spray
common_failure_modes.prevention: Stuff cans with paper and tape, or use can covers
common_failure_modes.remediation: Clean paint from can interior before trim installation

common_failure_modes.cause: Dry edge where ceiling meets wall
common_failure_modes.prevention: Maintain wet edge through transition, proper technique
common_failure_modes.remediation: Light sand and reprime affected area

common_failure_modes.cause: Drywall dust contamination, primer applied too thick
common_failure_modes.prevention: Thorough vacuum of both surfaces, proper application technique

common_failure_modes.cause: Different absorption rates between joint compound and paper face
common_failure_modes.prevention: Use high-build primer for Level 3 drywall, consider double prime
common_failure_modes.remediation: Additional primer coat, consider high-build product

notes_for_materials_manager: PVA primer is default for QT2-QT3, acrylic latex for QT4
Coverage rates: ~350 SF/gal smooth, ~275 SF/gal textured, ~200 SF/gal high-build
Combined ceiling+wall SF drives material quantity - calculate as single total
NO floor protection materials needed - subfloor only in NC pre-trim
Masking film for window/door openings - 72-99 inch width typical
Plastic sheeting (0.35 mil) for building materials covering
Paper/tape for electrical boxes and recessed lighting protection
5-gallon containers standard for NC production volumes
notes_for_sop_librarian: Surface sequencing is CRITICAL: Ceilings FIRST, then Walls
No formal edge work modules needed - both surfaces get same coat
Vacuum step is CRITICAL - drywall dust causes adhesion failure on both surfaces
NO spot-prime fasteners task - galvanized screws do not rust in normal NC timeline
NO floor protection task - subfloor only in pre-trim phase
Spray+backroll modules need coupling constraint (backroll sets pace)
Protection setup must complete BEFORE any primer application
Maintain wet edge at ceiling-wall transition (technique, not separate task)
Protection tasks use room-based heuristics, not per-fixture counts
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Combined SF (ceiling + wall) is the quantity driver for application tasks
Roll rates: ~350 SF/hr smooth walls, ~300 SF/hr ceilings (overhead factor)
Spray rates: ~600-700 SF/hr but limited by backroll if using spray+backroll
Effective spray+backroll rate is backroll rate (coupling constraint)
No edge work labor - significant time savings vs separate ceiling/wall specs
No floor protection labor - subfloor only in NC pre-trim
Protection tasks use room count with heuristics (electrical 8-12/room, lights 4-8/room)
assumptions: All drywall is standard gypsum board (not specialized types)
New construction surface condition is 'Good' - minimal defects expected
Standard ceiling heights 8-10 ft (adjust rates for higher ceilings)
Drywall contractor has completed all taping, mudding, and sanding
Galvanized drywall screws used (no rust during normal timeline)
Subfloor only - no finished flooring installed yet
No remediation of drywall damage in scope (painter responsible for prime only)
Adequate ventilation available for primer dry time
Windows may be installed but interior doors not yet hung
Pre-trim phase - no baseboard, casing, crown molding installed
uncertainties: Drywall finish quality varies by contractor - may need field adjustment to prep scope
Number of electrical boxes per room can vary significantly (8-12 is average estimate)
Number of recessed lights per room varies by design (4-8 is average estimate)
Whether exterior doors are installed or just rough openings
Impact of humidity on dry times between ceiling and wall phases
